results.answer: Primary-payer class, including voided claims. blues: claims 411, avg lag 11.16 days, median 4.00, submitted >90 days after service 7; commercial: claims 710, avg lag 7.02 days, median 4.00, submitted >90 days after service 1; medicaid: claims 55, avg lag 11.45 days, median 4.00, submitted >90 days after service 1; medicaid_mco: claims 241, avg lag 10.78 days, median 4.00, submitted >90 days after service 5; medicare: claims 509, avg lag 4.97 days, median 3.00, submitted >90 days after service 0; medicare_advantage: claims 363, avg lag 7.10 days, median 4.00, submitted >90 days after service 1; other: claims 47, avg lag 5.15 days, median 3.00, submitted >90 days after service 0. Assumption: population is claims with a primary 837 (payer_responsibility P); secondary-only claims are out. Lag is earliest submission to any payer minus date of service (service date does not vary across a claim's submissions). Payer class is the primary payer's class. Average rounded to 2 decimals; median is the continuous median rounded to 2 decimals; the >90 count is strict.
results.final_sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT claim_key, min(submission_date) AS first_submission, min(service_date_from) AS service_date
  FROM sem.claims GROUP BY 1
), primary_class AS (
  SELECT claim_key, min(payer_class) AS payer_class
  FROM sem.claims WHERE payer_responsibility = 'P' GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT pc.payer_class, count(*) AS claims,
       round(avg(date_diff('day', b.service_date, b.first_submission)), 2) AS avg_lag_days,
       round(median(date_diff('day', b.service_date, b.first_submission)), 2) AS median_lag_days,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE date_diff('day', b.service_date, b.first_submission) > 90) AS claims_over_90
FROM base b JOIN primary_class pc USING (claim_key)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

results.answer: Days to pay by primary payer class: blues: paid claims 188, median 18.0 days, 90th percentile 22.0 days; commercial: paid claims 313, median 16.0 days, 90th percentile 24.0 days; medicaid: paid claims 24, median 22.0 days, 90th percentile 29.4 days; medicaid_mco: paid claims 87, median 27.0 days, 90th percentile 31.4 days; medicare: paid claims 289, median 17.0 days, 90th percentile 20.0 days; medicare_advantage: paid claims 184, median 21.0 days, 90th percentile 26.0 days; other: paid claims 16, median 23.5 days, 90th percentile 31.0 days. Assumption: keep current adjudications from the primary payer (837 payer_responsibility P) with paid_amount > 0. Days = that payment date minus the first 837 submission date to the same payer. Median and 90th percentile are continuous/linear, rounded to 1 decimal. Payer class is the primary payer's class.
results.final_sql:
WITH prim AS (
  SELECT claim_key, payer_key, min(payer_class) AS payer_class, min(submission_date) AS first_submission
  FROM sem.claims WHERE payer_responsibility = 'P' GROUP BY 1, 2
), paid AS (
  SELECT claim_key, payer_key, payment_date
  FROM sem.remit_claims
  WHERE is_current_adjudication AND paid_amount > 0
)
SELECT p.payer_class, count(*) AS paid_claims,
       round(quantile_cont(date_diff('day', p.first_submission, r.payment_date), 0.5), 1) AS median_days,
       round(quantile_cont(date_diff('day', p.first_submission, r.payment_date), 0.9), 1) AS p90_days
FROM prim p JOIN paid r USING (claim_key, payer_key)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

results.answer: Top 5 CO reviewed-denial CARCs by denied claim+payer count: 197 (12 denied claim+payers); 16 (11 denied claim+payers); 18 (9 denied claim+payers); 55 (9 denied claim+payers); 96 (8 denied claim+payers). Assumption: current adjudications that are denied; adjustments in group CO with is_denial_carc; each denied claim+payer counted once per CARC; rank by that count, ties broken by CARC code ascending.
results.final_sql:
SELECT a.carc_code, count(DISTINCT a.remit_claim_id) AS denied_claim_payers
FROM sem.adjustments a
JOIN sem.remit_claims r ON r.remit_claim_id = a.remit_claim_id
WHERE r.is_current_adjudication AND r.is_denied AND a.group_code = 'CO' AND a.is_denial_carc
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC, 1 LIMIT 5

results.answer: First-pass resolution by payer class: blues: remitted pairs 406, first-pass 370, rate 91.13%; commercial: remitted pairs 680, first-pass 628, rate 92.35%; medicaid: remitted pairs 81, first-pass 78, rate 96.30%; medicaid_mco: remitted pairs 255, first-pass 239, rate 93.73%; medicare: remitted pairs 536, first-pass 515, rate 96.08%; medicare_advantage: remitted pairs 378, first-pass 353, rate 93.39%; other: remitted pairs 57, first-pass 54, rate 94.74%. Assumption: a claim+payer pair is in the population if it has any 835 claim payment. First pass means exactly one such event, that event is the current adjudication, and it is not a denial. Rate is first-pass pairs / remitted pairs as a percentage rounded to 2 decimals.
results.final_sql:
WITH pairs AS (
  SELECT payer_class, claim_key, payer_key, count(*) AS events,
         bool_or(is_current_adjudication) AS has_current,
         bool_or(is_denied) AS any_denied
  FROM sem.remit_claims GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
)
SELECT payer_class, count(*) AS remitted_pairs,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE events = 1 AND has_current AND NOT any_denied) AS first_pass_pairs,
       round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE events = 1 AND has_current AND NOT any_denied) / count(*), 2) AS first_pass_rate_pct
FROM pairs GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

results.answer: 25 CO denial CARCs on denied current adjudications, ordered by pair count then CARC: 197: 12 pairs, $21,021.14; 16: 11 pairs, $11,343.78; 18: 9 pairs, $3,134.29; 55: 9 pairs, $15,966.55; 96: 8 pairs, $10,123.32; 183: 7 pairs, $4,516.19; 29: 6 pairs, $2,347.44; 97: 5 pairs, $364.03; 204: 4 pairs, $1,261.40; 22: 4 pairs, $2,400.27; 252: 4 pairs, $843.32; 15: 3 pairs, $9,079.64; 27: 3 pairs, $1,072.19; 50: 3 pairs, $9,079.64; B7: 3 pairs, $1,323.78; 198: 2 pairs, $1,238.57; 236: 2 pairs, $41.96; 24: 2 pairs, $479.73; 109: 1 pairs, $234.32; 119: 1 pairs, $515.01; 234: 1 pairs, $20.98; 242: 1 pairs, $234.32; 288: 1 pairs, $515.01; 4: 1 pairs, $6,872.90; B15: 1 pairs, $234.32. Assumption: claim and line adjustments, group CO, reviewed denial CARCs only (is_denial_carc); each denied claim+payer counted once per code; dollars are the sum of those adjustment amounts rounded to 2 decimals.
results.final_sql:
SELECT a.carc_code,
       count(DISTINCT a.claim_key || '|' || a.payer_key) AS denied_claim_payers,
       round(sum(a.adjustment_amount), 2) AS co_amount
FROM sem.adjustments a
JOIN sem.remit_claims r ON r.remit_claim_id = a.remit_claim_id
WHERE r.is_current_adjudication AND r.is_denied AND a.group_code = 'CO' AND a.is_denial_carc
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC, 1

results.answer: 327 billed procedure codes. Each row is procedure, top principal diagnosis, claims with that pair, claims with the procedure, and the pair's share in percent. First (procedure order): 36415 / Z0000, 178 of 1152 claims (15.5%). Last: G0483 / Z79891, 35 of 52 (67.3%). Assumption: one row per claim at its latest 837 submission, voids included; a claim counts once per CPT; the top diagnosis is the mode with ties broken by the lowest diagnosis code; share is rounded to 1 decimal percent.
results.final_sql:
WITH lines AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT c.claim_key, cl.procedure_code, c.principal_diagnosis_code
  FROM sem.claim_lines cl
  JOIN sem.claims c ON c.claim_id = cl.claim_id
  WHERE c.is_latest_submission
),
pair AS (
  SELECT procedure_code, principal_diagnosis_code, count(*) AS n FROM lines GROUP BY 1, 2
),
tot AS (
  SELECT procedure_code, count(*) AS total_claims FROM lines GROUP BY 1
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT procedure_code, principal_diagnosis_code, n,
         row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY procedure_code ORDER BY n DESC, principal_diagnosis_code ASC) AS rn
  FROM pair
)
SELECT r.procedure_code, r.principal_diagnosis_code, r.n AS claims_with_top_dx, t.total_claims,
       round(100.0 * r.n / t.total_claims, 1) AS top_dx_share_pct
FROM ranked r JOIN tot t USING (procedure_code)
WHERE r.rn = 1
ORDER BY 1

Explore: 22 shared probes (view counts, payer-name dictionary, null rates, frequency, DOS stability, join cardinality of primary 837 to current 835) before the candidates.
